detail: SP-025's D-71 review (low, informational): (1) a Developer ID build could also require 'anchor apple generic and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = <team>', so a planted ad-hoc bundle fails where the real app is Developer ID signed; (2) the genuine app can be started by an agent with ORCH_SOCKET or ORCH_DATA_DIR aimed at its own fake daemon (open --env, launchctl setenv), showing the user an agent's data to approve: release builds could ignore those variables or check orchd's signature on the socket; (3) a terminal with Accessibility permission can drive the app's buttons through System Events (SP-077's confirmation should show which terminal asked); (4) builds without cgo, and Linux, recognize no Orch.app, so under a policy no caller is the operator there and the policy can be changed only by editing orch.db with orchd stopped.
